chunks: Humayd ibn Ziyad from Ibn Sama'ah from Ibn Jabala and Ali ibn Muhammad from Salih ibn Abi Hammad from Abdullah ibn Jabala from Abdullah ibn Sinan from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said:

Slaughter for him (the newborn), and shave his head on the seventh day, and give in charity silver equal to the weight of his hair, and cut the Aqeeqa meat into pieces, and cook it, and invite a group of Muslims to eat it.

key_terms.رَهْطاً: A group or party of people
key_terms.عَقَّ: Slaughter of an animal for a newborn child (Aqeeqa)

ai.seo_question: What are the specific rituals and obligations for a newborn child in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the Sunnah of Aqeeqa on the seventh day, linking the ritual sacrifice to the shaving of the head and the distribution of silver equivalent to the hair's weight, a practice emphasizing gratitude and purification. It further details the preparation of the meat as a communal feast, inviting relatives and Muslims to share in the blessing, thereby reinforcing social bonds and charity within the Shia tradition.

en.hubeali:
Humeyd Bin Ziyad, from Ibn Sama’at, from Ibn Jabala and Ali Bin Muhammad, from Salih Bin Abu Hammad, from Abdullah Bin jabala, from Abdullah Bin Sinan, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘

Perform Aqeeqa for him (new-born) and shave off his head on the seventh day, and give silver in charity by the weight of his hair, and cut the Aqeeqa (slaughtered meat) in pieces and cook it, and invite over it a group from the Muslims’.
en.sarwar: 1. Humayd ibn Ziyad has narrated from ibn Sama‘ah from ibn Jabalah and Ali ibn Muhammad has narrated from Salih ibn abu Hammad from ‘Abd Allah ibn Jabalah from ‘Abd Allah ibn Sinan who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has stated this Hadith.

‘On the seventh day from birth offer ‘Aqiqah, shave the head of the child and give in charity an amount of silver equal to the weight of his hairs and cut the meat of Aqiqah without breaking any bones, then cook the meat and invite a group of Muslims to be served.’”
